suggestion.rationale: Article quantifies: '162,275 packages related to mobile banking Trojans' detected in Q1 2026. Baseline detection for banking malware families is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create behavioral signatures for banking trojan families (SparkCat, Triada, Keenadu derivatives). Flag apps requesting PERMISSION_GET_ACCOUNTS, PERMISSION_READ_SMS, or PERMISSION_CALL_LOG that also make outbound HTTPS connections to non-CDN infrastructure. Monitor for process memory allocation patterns consistent with dynamic code loading in banking app context.

suggestion.title: Triada and Keenadu Trojan Reactivation Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata tags explicitly list 'Triada, Keenadu' as Q1 2026 threats. These are historically significant mobile trojans requiring continuous surveillance baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for behavioral signatures and code artifacts from Triada (known for privilege escalation via CVE exploits) and Keenadu (known for SMS interception). Flag apps executing su/doas binaries, accessing /dev/kmem, or hooking system libraries. Monitor for SMS access patterns with exfiltration to external HTTP endpoints.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Rust Mobile Malware Library Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'The obfuscated malicious Rust library was decrypted using a Dalvik-like virtual machine.' Rust-based malware is emerging; requires signature-independent detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Rust-compiled shared objects (.so files) with high entropy and custom packer signatures. Flag runtime unpacking of Rust binaries (signature: Rust panic infrastructure or DWARF debug sections). Monitor for SIGSEGV and signal handler manipulation patterns used in anti-debugging by Rust payloads.

suggestion.title: RCE Exploitation Against Public-Facing Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article title lists RCE as patch category across Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP, VMware, n8n; no initial-access detections generated. RCE implies unauthenticated or minimally-authenticated network-accessible vulnerability exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to known vulnerable endpoints in Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP, VMware, n8n management UIs with command injection payloads, path traversal, or serialization gadgets. Monitor for process spawning or reverse shells from web service accounts immediately following suspicious HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection in Database-Backed Applications
suggestion.rationale: Article title cites SQL injection as discrete vulnerability class; zero execution-phase detections. SQL injection indicates exploitable database query construction in web/API layers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect UNION-based, time-based blind, or error-based SQL payloads in HTTP parameters. Monitor database process logs for anomalous table enumeration (information_schema, pg_catalog queries), privilege escalation (ALTER ROLE, CREATE USER), or high-volume SELECT statements from unexpected sources.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists privilege escalation flaws as patch category; no escalation-phase detections. Common post-RCE/SQLi escalation vector to achieve system-level compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SYSTEM/root process spawning from service accounts, privileged token theft (SeImpersonate, SeDebug), UAC/sudo bypass syscalls, or setuid binary abuse. Detect kernel exploitation patterns or capability abuse (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN).

suggestion.title: Ivanti VPN/Access Product Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Ivanti explicitly named in title with RCE/SQL/privilege escalation flaws; zero product-specific IOCs or detections. Ivanti Connect Secure, Endpoint Manager, and mobilIron products are externally accessible and frequently targeted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti gateway/management ports for exploitation attempts via cgi-bin path traversal, authentication bypass payloads, or known gadget chains. Detect unusual process spawning (perl, bash, python) from Ivanti service accounts or unexpected outbound connections from VPN appliance.

suggestion.title: FortiGate SSL-VPN and Web UI Attacks
suggestion.rationale: Fortinet explicitly in title but zero product-specific detections. FortiGate is globally deployed; SSL-VPN and administrative UI are RCE-prone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiGate /api/v2, /ng, /admin interfaces with command injection payloads (.cgi fuzzing, template injection in logs/alerts). Monitor for shell spawning (bash, /bin/sh) from Fortinet daemon processes or unexpected SSH/telnet connections to FortiGate from external IPs.

suggestion.title: n8n Workflow Execution Engine Abuse
suggestion.rationale: n8n explicitly cited with RCE; no detections generated. n8n is JavaScript/Node.js execution engine; workflow deserialization or Node code injection leads to arbitrary process execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor n8n node processes for unexpected child spawning (shell, python, curl), file writes to /tmp or workflow directories with .js/.json payloads, or outbound connections to attacker infrastructure. Detect prototype pollution or deserialization payloads in workflow definition uploads.

suggestion.title: Windows Event Log Detection: Error Code 0x800f0922
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names error code 0x800f0922 as the failure indicator. Pipeline should extract and hunt for this error code in Windows event logs (event ID 20, 24, 25 in System log during update operations).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on EventID matching Windows Update failure patterns with error code 0x800f0922. Look for recurring failures on the same system or across cohort indicating supply-chain or targeted update attack. Correlate with post-update anomalies (process execution, registry changes, service disablement).

suggestion.title: Abnormal Windows Update Failure Rate Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article describes widespread update failure [HIGH]. Cohort-level detection of Update failure rate exceeding baseline by 2-3x within 1h window indicates coordinated delivery failure or adversary-induced update blocking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate failed update count by device/OU per hour. Trigger alert if failure rate ≥2x baseline OR >30% of fleet fails same error code within rolling 2h window. Correlate with time of official Microsoft advisory to distinguish legitimate known-issue from active attack.

suggestion.title: Post-Update Suspicious Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Windows update failures often precede exploitation attempts by adversaries seeking to exploit unpatched or partially-patched systems. Detect unusual process execution within 10min post-update-failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Windows Update failure event with anomalous child process spawning from winlogon/svchost within 600sec window. Look for cmdline containing script interpreters (powershell.exe, cmd.exe /c, cscript.exe) or binary downloads (certutil, curl, wget). Alert if spawned process has known malware hash.

suggestion.title: Windows Update Service Tampering or Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Adversaries often disable or interfere with Windows Update (wuauserv) post-compromise. Detect attempts to stop, disable, or modify update service following reported update failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for net.exe/sc.exe commands targeting 'wuauserv' with 'stop', 'disable', 'config' parameters. Alert on registry modifications to HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\wuauserv (Start value set to 4=disabled). Correlate with Update failure events and user context (non-SYSTEM execution = higher confidence).

suggestion.title: Malicious Update Package Injection or Man-in-the-Middle
suggestion.rationale: Error 0x800f0922 could mask delivery of malicious update payload or MITM attack during update retrieval. Detect anomalous Windows Update traffic or certificate validation failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS certificate validation errors during WSUS/Windows Update communication. Detect unusual Windows Update traffic to non-Microsoft CDN/IP ranges. Look for HTTP responses with mismatch between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding during package download. Correlate with error 0x800f0922 and alert if update package hash fails verification.

suggestion.title: Rollback or Downgrade Following Update Failure
suggestion.rationale: Adversary may intentionally trigger update failure to trigger rollback, exposing system to known CVEs in earlier OS build. Detect rollback or intentional downgrade post-failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Windows version downgrades detected via WMI win32_operatingsystem.BuildNumber decreasing, or registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\CurrentBuildNumber value decreasing. Correlate with preceding update failure event and check if rollback was user-initiated vs. automatic. Flag automatic rollbacks post-0x800f0922 error as suspicious.

suggestion.title: VS Code Extension Marketplace Update with Subsequent C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes supply-chain delivery via extension auto-update. Need detection for extension process spawning network connections to non-standard registries/C2 post-update.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate VS Code extension update events (marketplaceServiceVSCode process or extensions/*/package.json write) with outbound DNS/HTTP from electron.exe or node.exe within 60 seconds to non-npm-registry ASNs or dynamic DNS providers.

suggestion.title: Malicious Node.js/JavaScript Execution from VS Code Extension Directory
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension runs JavaScript payload in Electron/Node context with full process privileges. Need behavioral detection for command spawning or file access from extension runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node.exe child process spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash with parent in .vscode/extensions/ directory. Also monitor for require()/dynamic module loading from /tmp or untrusted paths during extension initialization.

suggestion.title: SSH Key and Git Credential Access from Development Extension
suggestion.rationale: VS Code running in dev environment has direct filesystem access to ~/.ssh, ~/.git, ~/.aws, .vscode/settings.json with stored tokens and credentials. Compromised extension can exfiltrate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file read access from electron.exe/node.exe to ~/.ssh/*, ~/.aws/credentials, .git/config, or .vscode/settings.json. Correlate reads with subsequent outbound connections (base64-encoded POST or DNS exfil tunnels).

suggestion.title: C2 Command and Control from Electron/Node Process
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extension beacons to attacker infrastructure for command relay, credential staging, or data exfil. Need DNS and HTTP/HTTPS pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DNS queries from node.exe to newly registered domains (WHOIS registration <7 days old relative to first query) or to IPs in bulletproof hosting/botnet ASNs. Track HTTP User-Agent strings typical of Node.js or custom exfil tools.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Extension Version Change or Lateral Install Across Workspace
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack may propagate to shared dev environment via .vscode/extensions/ sync or devcontainer.json; need detection for unauthorized extension adds or version downgrades.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on extensions.json modifications adding new extensions without user action, or .vscode/extensions/ directory changes occurring outside of IDE update/install UI. Flag extension version downgrades (e.g., Nx Console rollback to pre-fix version).

suggestion.title: Fast16 Malware Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Fast16 Malware'—pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Any malware family name in a HIGH-severity advisory is a primary detection indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution events referencing 'Fast16' malware family, known variants, or associated process names. Cross-reference against threat-intel feeds for sample hashes, parent-process chains, and command-line indicators from pre-Stuxnet malware campaign.

suggestion.title: Nuclear Simulation Software Tampering via File Write Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'tampered with nuclear weapons simulations'—this is direct impact-phase activity. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this clear attack description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file modifications to nuclear simulation software directories (binaries, DLLs, configuration files). Baseline legitimate simulation updates, then flag modifications from non-standard processes, scheduled tasks, or processes with suspicious parent lineage or network access patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Injection into Simulation Applications
suggestion.rationale: Pre-Stuxnet malware typically used process injection for stealth and persistence in critical infrastructure. Article context implies sophisticated malware requiring injection techniques to survive simulation-environment auditing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process injection attempts (CreateRemoteThread, WriteProcessMemory, etc.) targeting simulation software processes. Correlate with suspicious parent processes, DLL loads from non-standard paths, and unsigned binaries. Alert if injection source has network connectivity or recent file-write activity to simulation directories.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Lateral Movement in Isolated Nuclear Facility Networks
suggestion.rationale: Fast16 targeting nuclear weapons simulations implies network-isolated critical infrastructure. Pipeline missed lateral-movement detections despite this infrastructure-specific context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for authorized lateral movement patterns in nuclear facility networks (approved admin jump-box hops, authorized service account migrations). Flag anomalies: unexpected RDP/SMB connections between simulation servers, traffic from non-standard source IPs, or connections at unusual times. Correlate with file-tampering alerts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Registry Persistence Modifications in Nuclear Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Pre-Stuxnet malware required persistent mechanisms to survive reboots in critical-infrastructure environments. Article provides no technical details but malware-tampering context implies local persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, RunOnce, and service-registry hives from non-standard processes. Alert on unusual timing (off-hours, during simulation maintenance windows), unsigned process origins, and modifications followed by network traffic or file tampering.

suggestion.title: Simulation Software Reconnaissance via File/Directory Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Malware targeting nuclear weapons simulations must first discover simulation software location, version, and dependencies. Article context implies reconnaissance phase precedes tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual file-enumeration patterns from unexpected processes querying simulation software directories, checking for specific DLLs, or enumerating network shares in nuclear facility networks. Correlate with API calls (FindFirstFile, RegEnumKeyEx) and flag if enumeration precedes file modifications or process injection.

suggestion.title: AppleScript execution via applescript:// URL handler with Script Editor
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'relies on the applescript:// URL scheme to launch the macOS Script Editor preloaded with a malicious AppleScript.' Direct evasion of Terminal-based mitigations in macOS Tahoe 26.4.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Script Editor (com.apple.ScriptEditor.app) launched with applescript:// protocol handler. Correlate with network egress, curl/zsh spawning, or LaunchAgent creation in same timeline.

suggestion.title: Malicious installer distribution via typosquatted domains
suggestion.rationale: Article names three active distribution domains: 'qq-0732gwh22[.]com, mlcrosoft[.]co[.]com, mlroweb[.]com' serving fake WeChat/Miro/Microsoft installers. Direct initial-access IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block/alert on DNS/HTTP to these three domains. Monitor for .dmg/.pkg downloads immediately post-resolution. Flag any successful connection attempt to mlcrosoft[.]co[.]com or qq-0732gwh22[.]com variants.

suggestion.title: LaunchAgent persistence masquerading as Google software update
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'installing a script impersonating the Google software update and registers it using LaunchAgent. The script is executed every minute and acts as a beacon.' Highly detectable persistence primitive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/Library/LaunchAgents for new .plist files created post-infection with 'Google', 'Update', or 'Apple' in the label. Correlate with /var/tmp, /tmp shell script references. Alert on minute-level beacon execution pattern from LaunchAgent-triggered process.

suggestion.title: Keychain credential theft via AppleScript password prompt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'prompts the user for their macOS password, which can then be used to access Keychain items, decrypt credentials, and access protected data.' Distinctive post-execution behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AppleScript or osascript execution that displays password dialogs. Cross-correlate with Keychain unlock operations (SecKeychainItemCopyContent, SecKeychainUnlock) in same user session within 30 seconds of prompt.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency wallet application hijacking via app.asar replacement
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hijacks them by terminating their processes and replacing the legitimate core application file with a malicious one called app.asar...clears the quarantine attributes with xattr -cr and uses ad hoc code signing.' Specific, detectable file replacement pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process termination of known wallet apps (Exodus, Ledger Live, Atomic Wallet, Electrum, Trezor Suite) followed by file write to app.asar in their .app bundle Contents/Resources/. Detect xattr -cr + ad-hoc codesign operations on .app bundles within 60s of wallet process kill.

suggestion.title: Device fingerprinting and geo-blocking via Russian keyboard detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'system check to determine if the victim uses a Russian keyboard/input, and if there's a match, it reports a cis_blocked event...and exits without infecting the system.' Unique pre-infection reconnaissance pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AppleScript/osascript execution that queries keyboard layouts, input sources, or locale settings. Detect early process exit or C2 beacon with 'cis_blocked', 'blocked', or locale-specific failure markers before payload execution.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Repository Tag Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'All Tags Point to Imposter Commit'—direct evidence of tag substitution attack. Pipeline extracted no use case despite this being the core attack method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected or unauthorized modifications to tags in Actions repositories, especially when all or most tags are updated to new commit hashes within a short timeframe. Correlate with commit authorship changes or API token usage patterns outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Credential Exfiltration from Actions
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Exfiltrates CI/CD Credentials'—core impact. No detection use case was generated despite this being the attacker's objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Actions workflows read GitHub secrets (via `secrets.*` or environment variables), followed by unexpected outbound HTTPS connections or POST requests to non-standard domains. Correlate secret access with unusual runner IP geolocation or credential staging in workflow logs.

suggestion.title: Malicious Commit Content in Actions Tags
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'imposter commit' injected into all tags. No detection covering commit content analysis or hash verification against expected baselines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For high-value Actions repositories, establish baseline commit hashes for each tag. Alert when tag-to-commit mapping diverges from baseline, or when commit diffs introduce new shell commands, environment variable exports, or HTTP requests not present in previous versions.

suggestion.title: Downstream Repository Consumption of Compromised Action
suggestion.rationale: Attackers gain access to all workflows using the compromised Action. No detection for identifying or monitoring downstream consumers of a known-compromised Actions tag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query GitHub API for all public and private repositories using `actions-cool/issues-helper@v*` or similar patterns. For repos using the compromised tag, cross-reference with recent credential exfiltration alerts, unusual secret access, or network anomalies. Prioritize repos with broad cloud access or deployment permissions.

suggestion.title: GitHub API Token or SSH Key Usage Anomalies in Actions Context
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack likely requires initial compromise via stolen credentials. No detection for abnormal API/SSH activity that may precede repository mutation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls or SSH operations against Actions repositories from unusual IPs, at unusual times, or with unusual patterns (e.g., bulk tag modifications, permission changes). Cross-correlate with GitHub's 'suspicious activity' notifications or failed 2FA attempts on maintainer accounts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation or Version Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks exploit package management. Article explicitly describes 'malicious node-ipc versions published to npm'—the entry point. No detection for abnormal package versions, unexpected installation, or registry tampering was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installations of node-ipc with versions outside normal ranges or from atypical timelines. Flag rapid package version downgrades post-patch or installations during off-hours. Cross-reference package version against npm security advisories in real-time.

suggestion.title: Node Process Performing Unexpected System Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware typically profiles the target system post-execution. Article describes malicious code execution via package import. No use case for discovery activity (process enumeration, user enumeration, cloud resource discovery) from Node.js processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js or npm processes spawning discovery utilities (Get-Process, whoami, id, aws sts get-caller-identity) or enumerating file system paths sensitive to credential storage (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, APPDATA). Flag unexpected process parent-child relationships (node → powershell, node → sh).

suggestion.title: Node Process Making Out-of-Band Network Connections to Non-Standard Ports
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages in supply chain attacks commonly exfiltrate data or establish C2 channels. Article establishes execution from imported malicious code but no detection for anomalous egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Node.js processes establishing connections to IPs/domains not in allowlist, especially on ports 22, 3389, 5985, 8443, or dynamic ranges. Correlate with package version timing and detect large data transfers to external IPs shortly after install.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Attempt Originating from Node Module Context
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromises often serve as pivot points. Article does not indicate detection for downstream attacks, credential theft, or lateral movement initiated from node_modules execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for lateral movement indicators originating from Node.js or npm processes: SMB/RDP connections to other hosts, Kerberos requests from unusual service accounts, or credential reuse from node_modules directories. Flag suspicious account enumeration preceding connection attempts.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration or File Access Anomaly from Node.js Process
suggestion.rationale: The article explicitly describes a supply chain attack; the intent is typically data theft or sabotage. No detection use case addresses unauthorized file access, credential harvesting, or exfiltration by malicious package code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes accessing sensitive file paths (SSH keys, .aws/credentials, browser cookies, git configs, environment files) or reading bulk data into memory. Correlate with network egress or piping to compression utilities. Flag access to files outside the package's declared dependencies.

suggestion.title: npm Lockfile or Dependency Tree Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Advanced supply chain attacks may target package.json, package-lock.json, or yarn.lock. Article references malicious published versions but does not surface detection for in-repo manifest tampering or integrity violations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to package-lock.json, package.json, or dependency version pinning. Detect commits that downgrade security patches or add unreviewed packages. Flag file modifications outside standard developer workflows (weekends, off-hours, from CI systems).

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation: Nx Console Version Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Compromised Nx Console 18.95.0'—detection must flag unexpected package versions, installations from non-official sources, or checksum mismatches. Title establishes the artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/yarn package manager logs for Nx Console installations. Flag version 18.95.0 specifically, unexpected downgrades, or downloads from repositories other than npmjs.com. Correlate with file hash validation against published npm registry checksums.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting: Suspicious Filesystem Access from VS Code Extension
suggestion.rationale: Title describes 'credential stealer' targeting 'VS Code developers'—attacker code must enumerate and read SSH keys, git credentials, .env files, or browser password databases. Requires detection of file access patterns from extension processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on code.exe/node.exe child processes reading ~/.ssh/*, ~/.aws/*, ~/.git/config, %APPDATA%\npm, or browser credential stores. Flag rapid sequential file opens from extension initialization context.

suggestion.title: Extension-Spawned C2 Callback: Outbound Network from VS Code
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer must exfiltrate stolen data ('credential stealer' in title implies C2 communication). Detect suspicious outbound HTTPS from VS Code to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS connections from code.exe to newly registered domains (WHOIS <30 days), high-entropy subdomains, or non-standard ports. Correlate with credential access file operations and POST/PUT payloads.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Cascade: Unauthorized Git Operations from Compromised Developer Machines
suggestion.rationale: Once developer credentials are stolen via the malicious extension, attacker uses them to compromise downstream repositories and CI/CD systems. Detect anomalous git pushes/API token usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub/GitLab for git push operations from new geolocations, unusual times, or high-permission token usage. Flag API token grants to new OAuth applications or unexpected CI/CD pipeline executions.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Extension Initialization: Suspicious Code Patterns in Nx Console Package
suggestion.rationale: Legitimate package compromised with malicious extension code must hide intent. Detect obfuscation, dynamic code evaluation, or suspicious imports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Static analysis of nx-console extension code: flag base64-encoded strings, eval/Function constructor usage, undeclared child_process or net module calls, or suspicious environment variable access during activation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Entra ID Sign-In from Impossible Travel or Unfamiliar Device
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Entra ID account abuse'—core indicator of credential compromise; pipeline failed to suggest detection of anomalous authentication tied to exfiltration activity
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Entra ID sign-ins from impossible travel origins or new device identities with subsequent M365/Azure data access. Flag logins from attacker infrastructure IP ranges, residential proxies, or geographies inconsistent with user baseline.

suggestion.title: New OAuth App Registration with Mail.Read or Teams Access
suggestion.rationale: Attackers persist via service principal backdoors after compromising Entra ID; article describes sustained exfiltration implying persistence mechanism; pipeline did not surface application layer persistence detections
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registration of applications granting Directory.Read.All, Mail.ReadWrite, Chat.ReadWrite, or Teams.ReadWrite scopes. Correlate creation timestamp with suspicious Entra ID account activity and subsequent mailbox/Teams access patterns.

suggestion.title: Bulk Mailbox and Teams Collection via Automated Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'exfiltrate Microsoft 365 data'; pipeline missed the collection phase—the attack flow requires accessing and exfiling mailbox contents and Teams conversations
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume MailItemsAccessed events from service principal or unfamiliar user context, PST exports, mail forwarding to external domains, or bulk Teams channel enumeration. Flag exfiltration via OAuth app with delegated mail permissions.

suggestion.title: Conditional Access Policy Weakening or MFA Bypass Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Attackers evade defenses to maintain persistent exfiltration; article implies sustained capability despite Azure/M365 security controls—defense evasion must have occurred
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for deletion, modification, or exception-addition to conditional access policies, disabling of legacy authentication blocks, or MFA requirement removals. Alert on exclusions granted to newly-registered apps or service principals.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Azure Subscription via Compromised Entra ID Token
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Azure Data' exfiltration alongside M365—indicates pivot from Entra ID to IaaS resources; pipeline did not suggest Azure lateral movement detections
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API calls to Azure resource management, key vaults, storage accounts, or databases from Entra ID tokens with anomalous context (service principal, unfamiliar IP, time outside business hours). Correlate with simultaneous M365 exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Data Export and Exfiltration Over Web Service from Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes exfiltration outcome; missing detection for the final exfiltration channel—suspicious download/export of bulk M365/Azure data via web service or cloud sync
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk downloads of mail archives, SharePoint files, or Azure data to external cloud services (OneDrive personal, Dropbox, Google Drive) or uploads to attacker-controlled domains. Monitor for zip/tar creation and upload patterns from compromised accounts.

suggestion.title: Automated Vulnerability Discovery via AI Model Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Automated Vulnerability Research' — pipeline extracted zero use cases for detecting automated fuzzing, scanning, or vulnerability discovery patterns that would precede PoC generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained high-velocity process spawning indicative of fuzzing frameworks or automated vulnerability scanning tools. Look for parent processes launching child processes with scanning/fuzzing characteristics (repeated file operations, network probes) at non-human cadence. Focus on development tools launching unusual child processes or large batches of throwaway processes.

suggestion.title: Mass PoC Exploit Code Generation and Compilation
suggestion.rationale: Article centerpiece is 'Preview Builds PoC Exploits' — no use case generated for detecting mass production of compiled exploit artifacts or unusual compilation/build patterns indicative of automated exploit crafting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on patterns of rapid executable/shellcode generation followed by test execution. Look for compilers or script interpreters spawning unusual child processes at scale, creation of files with exploit-like patterns (shellcode bytes, ROP gadgets), or rapid iteration cycles of build-test-iterate without human interaction pace.

suggestion.title: AI Model Inference for Code Generation and Vulnerability Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Mythos' as AI system building exploits — missing detection for unusual GPU/ML compute resource utilization or inferencing patterns that would characterize AI models discovering and exploiting vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained GPU compute utilization or high memory pressure on development systems paired with file I/O patterns consistent with model weights or checkpoint loading. Detect execution of ML inference frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow) in non-training contexts with unusual code generation outputs.

suggestion.title: Bulk Exploit Distribution and Repository Publishing
suggestion.rationale: PoC exploits built at scale require distribution — article likely discusses publication mechanisms but pipeline generated zero use cases for detecting mass uploads to GitHub, GitLab, or underground repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk git pushes or repository commits containing exploit artifacts. Alert on unusual GitHub API activity from development systems (mass PR creation, repo provisioning), suspicious patterns of public exploit repository creation, or exfiltration of PoC code to external version control systems.

suggestion.title: Unusual Development Velocity and Build System Automation
suggestion.rationale: Automated PoC generation implies non-human development pace — pipeline missed detection for build pipeline anomalies, CI/CD job scaling, or containerized execution patterns that would indicate automated multi-variant exploit generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor build systems and CI/CD pipelines for non-standard job execution patterns, unusual scaling (docker/container spawning at 100x normal rate), or parameterized builds generating distinct variants at machine scale. Detect container orchestration events indicating mass parallel job execution.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Tool Integration — Mythos Framework Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article introduces 'Mythos' as a named tool capable of automated exploitation — pipeline extracted no IOCs for tool binary names, configuration files, GitHub repositories, or command-line signatures that would indicate threat actor deployment or red-team use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish IOC set for Mythos tool (binary names, configuration directories, command-line patterns, GitHub URLs if source available). Alert on execution of Mythos framework, presence of tool artifacts in temp/staging directories, or command patterns consistent with automated PoC framework invocation.

suggestion.title: Malicious Extension Network Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: Compromised Nx Console extension implies C2 channel from VS Code process. Article describes attack but no detection for abnormal extension network activity extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node.exe child processes of VS Code for outbound connections to non-Microsoft domains. Extension should only contact official package registries and Nx APIs. Alert on connections to newly-registered domains, unusual ports, or known malware C2 infrastructure from extension runtime.

suggestion.title: Developer Credential Exfiltration from VS Code
suggestion.rationale: Extension executes with user privileges and can read SSH keys, API tokens, .env files. Article implies threat but no use case for credential access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when VS Code extension node process reads ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube directories or files matching *env*, *token*, *key* patterns. Monitor for child process spawning (git credential, aws-cli) or environment variable enumeration from extension context.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Extension Installation or Replacement
suggestion.rationale: Article describes compromised extension in marketplace supply chain. No detection for malicious extension installation or legitimate extension replacement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .vscode/extensions directory for unexpected modifications, unsigned extensions, or version downgrades. Alert when VS Code extension API receives install requests for extensions matching known-malicious publisher accounts or from non-official marketplace sources.

suggestion.title: Command Execution from VS Code Extension Context
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension can spawn shells or execute system commands via Node.js child_process. No use case for detecting abnormal process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node.exe spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or /bin/sh from VS Code extension directory. Extension should not execute system shells. Monitor for one-liners containing reverse-shell payloads, data exfiltration commands, or privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Source Code and Project Exfiltration via Compromised Extension
suggestion.rationale: Extension has access to all open files in IDE workspace. Attack implies theft of proprietary code. No detection for bulk file reads or compression/encoding prior to exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume sequential file reads of source code files (.ts, .js, .java, .py) by VS Code extension. Alert on gzip/tar/zip creation in temp directories by extension, or base64 encoding of file contents in stdout/network traffic.

suggestion.title: Tampered Extension Manifest or Package Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack requires modification of extension publisher identity or malicious version signatures in marketplace. No IOC extraction suggests missing manifest validation logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate Nx Console extension package.json and publisher account against baseline. Alert on mismatched code signatures, unexpected dependency versions, or publisher account takeover indicators (geographic login anomalies, new API tokens).

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Tag Reference Pointing to Unverified Commit Hash
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Popular GitHub Action Tags Redirected to Imposter Commit'—the core attack vector. Detection must catch tag references that resolve to commits outside the official release history or that lack upstream repository provenance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor workflow files for action@tag references where the resolved commit SHA does not match the official upstream tag or where the tag was recently mutated. Alert on workflows using short SHAs (e.g., actions/checkout@abc1234) without corresponding tagged releases in the source repository.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Secret Exfiltration from GitHub Actions Workflow Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle explicitly states 'Steal CI/CD Credentials.' Imposter actions execute in workflow context with access to GITHUB_TOKEN, deployment keys, and other secrets. Detect environment variable access and exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on step logs containing credential dumps (printenv, env, echo $GITHUB_TOKEN, cat ~/.aws/credentials), base64-encoded token strings, or outbound HTTP POST/PUT to non-GitHub domains during workflow execution carrying secret-shaped data.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Artifact Push During Compromised CI/CD Workflow Execution
suggestion.rationale: Compromised workflow can inject malicious code into build artifacts (container images, npm packages, binaries) published to registries. Article targets 'popular' actions, implying widespread downstream impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package/container registries for artifacts published from unusual CI/CD identities, unsigned artifacts from normally-signed publishers, or version bumps without corresponding code commits in the official repository.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Exploitation Against Avada Builder Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'SQL Injection Flaws' in Avada Builder plugin. Pipeline should detect SQL injection attempts on plugin-specific endpoints; none generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server logs for SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, FROM, WHERE) in query strings targeting /wp-content/plugins/avada-builder/* paths. Correlate with 5xx errors or database connection errors. Watch for time-based blind SQL injection delays (sleep, benchmark functions).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated File Read from Avada Builder Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'File Read' vulnerability. Pipeline should generate detection for unauthorized access to plugin files; no use case produced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated HTTP requests returning 200 OK from /wp-content/plugins/avada-builder/ with file extensions (.php, .inc, .config). Monitor for requests lacking WordPress nonce headers or admin authentication. Flag requests exfiltrating configuration files or data files.

suggestion.title: Bulk Database Exfiltration via Compromised Plugin
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection + file read vulnerabilities enable data extraction at scale. Article cites 1M+ affected sites—impact should include collection/exfiltration detection not covered in empty output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusually large result sets returned from database queries originating from Avada Builder plugin processes. Track exported .csv/.json/.sql files written to web-accessible directories. Correlate high-volume SELECT queries with subsequent HTTP transfers of large payloads.

suggestion.title: Avada Builder Plugin Version Enumeration and Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: 1M sites running vulnerable plugin versions implies version discovery. Pipeline missed initial reconnaissance step needed to identify vulnerable targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to Avada Builder version-disclosure endpoints (readme.txt, version files) or requests to known vulnerable paths that only exist in affected versions. Flag systematic probing across multiple targets checking plugin presence.

suggestion.title: n8n Workflow Code Injection and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Critical n8n Vulnerabilities Expose Automation Nodes to Full RCE.' RCE implies attacker-controlled code execution via workflow definition manipulation or malicious nodes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning (bash, powershell, node child_process) from n8n daemon or container context. Alert on dynamic expression evaluation in workflows executing system commands. Correlate workflow modification events with subsequent process execution.

suggestion.title: n8n Unauthorized API Access for Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Full RCE requires system-level access. Attackers likely escalate privileges through n8n API or direct database manipulation of role assignments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect n8n API calls assigning admin roles, creating service principals, or querying credential vaults from non-admin accounts. Alert on direct database writes to user_role or credentials tables outside normal workflows.

suggestion.title: n8n HTTP Node Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Once code execution achieved, attackers use n8n's HTTP/webhook nodes to exfiltrate data via external callbacks. Article title emphasizes full RCE—implies data access and extraction capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP nodes targeting high-risk domains, bulk payload transfers (>1MB), or DNS queries to newly registered/suspicious subdomains. Correlate with workflow deployment events and code injection indicators.

suggestion.title: n8n Credential Theft via Workflow Introspection
suggestion.rationale: RCE attackers enumerate and steal stored credentials (API keys, database passwords, OAuth tokens) from n8n credential store. This is a direct attack on cloud-connected infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on workflows accessing the n8n credential store outside normal automation context. Monitor for bulk credential enumeration, decryption of stored secrets, or API calls to list/read credentials from unauthorized service accounts.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via DirtyDecrypt/DirtyCBC Kernel Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploit 'allows attackers to gain root access' on affected Linux systems via rxgk_decrypt_skb vulnerability. This is the primary attack vector and received zero detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged processes (uid>0) that transition to root (uid=0) execution context on CONFIG_RXGK-enabled systems (Fedora, Arch Linux, openSUSE Tumbleweed). Correlate with local execution of compiled exploit code within 60 seconds prior. Alert on abnormal kernel interactions (rxgk_decrypt_skb syscalls) from non-AFS-client processes.

suggestion.title: Detection of DirtyDecrypt PoC Compilation and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'proof-of-concept exploit' in poc.c form tested on Fedora, with 'Exploit available' status indicating weaponized code in the wild. Pipeline missed execution detection despite explicit poc.c reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on compilation of source files containing keywords: 'DirtyDecrypt', 'DirtyCBC', 'rxgk_decrypt_skb', 'COW guard'. Flag gcc/clang invocation with output targeting /tmp, /dev/shm, or current directory. Execution of compiled output within 60 seconds of compilation is high-confidence exploit staging.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Manipulation - esp4/esp6/rxrpc Unload Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Mitigation strategy explicitly prescribes: 'rmmod esp4 esp6 rxrpc'. Rapid sequential unloading of all three modules is anomalous in production and indicates either exploit preparation or defensive hardening. Pipeline generated no pattern-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when all three kernel modules (esp4, esp6, rxrpc) are unloaded within 90-second window by root/system account. Suspicious if sequence is initiated from application context or non-system service. Correlate with prior suspicious binary execution or privilege escalation events.

suggestion.title: RxGK Syscall Anomalies from Unprivileged Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability in 'missing COW guard in rxgk_decrypt_skb' function. RxGK is AFS security subsystem; syscalls targeting rxgk functions from non-AFS-client processes indicate exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor syscalls targeting rxgk-related kernel functions from processes outside AFS client (afsd, kafs). Alert on direct memory manipulation, copy-on-write (COW) bypass patterns, or kernel address-space access from user context. Focus on systems with CONFIG_RXGK enabled.

suggestion.title: Exploit Availability Detection - CVE-2026-31635 PoC Download
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'proof-of-concept exploit...now has a' public availability and testing on Fedora. Pipeline missed download-based threat hunting despite explicit PoC release announcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads of DirtyDecrypt, DirtyCBC, or CVE-2026-31635-related artifacts from GitHub, exploit databases, or threat repositories. Flag suspicious filenames (poc.c, poc, dirty*.c, dirtydecrypt*) landing in /tmp, /dev/shm, Downloads, or user homedirs on vulnerable Linux distros. Time-of-download correlate with active threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Cache Drop Detection - Post-Exploitation Defense Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article mitigation includes explicit command: 'echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'. Writing to drop_caches (synchronous kernel cache flush) requires elevated privileges, is non-standard on production systems, and correlates with post-exploitation cleanup or system hardening.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches with value '3' from root context. Benign in container initialization; suspicious on user workstations/servers. Correlate with prior execution of unknown/suspicious binaries, kernel module operations, or privilege escalation events within 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: Non-admin principal accessing /api/customize/git-repositories endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states eight endpoints 'never call the che[ckUserPermissions]' authorization check, allowing 'non-admin users to exfiltrate stored Git credentials.' Successful requests to these normally-admin-only endpoints by non-admin principals directly demonstrate the vulnerability being exploited.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful HTTP requests to /api/customize/git-repositories/* (list, get, create, update, delete, test, listBranches, browseFiles) by non-admin principals. Baseline: these endpoints should return 403 for non-admin; any 200/201 response indicates authorization bypass exploitation.

suggestion.title: Rapid enumeration-then-access on git repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker workflow: enumerate repositories (list, get), then verify credential access (test, browseFiles). Article's own UC_21_2 proposes detecting PUT followed by test/branches/files within 5 minutes as suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-admin user issuing GET /api/customize/git-repositories/{id} or POST /api/customize/git-repositories/*/test, followed within 5 minutes by GET /api/customize/git-repositories/*/branches or */files. Pattern indicates systematic credential discovery.

suggestion.title: Outbound Git/SSH from Arcane Backend to unapproved hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article warns exfiltrated credentials enable attackers to 'tamper with GitOps configs.' Detection catches Arcane Backend using stolen credentials to reach Git hosts outside approved providers. Article's UC_21_3 proposes this hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Arcane Backend processes for outbound SSH (port 22) or HTTPS (port 443) to IP/domain combinations outside approved Git providers (GitHub, GitLab, BitBucket, Azure DevOps). Flag any non-standard Git host connections.

suggestion.title: DELETE /api/customize/git-repositories by non-admin user
suggestion.rationale: Article describes DELETE endpoint enabling post-exfiltration cleanup or GitOps sabotage. This authorization bypass allows non-admin destruction of repository configurations. Article's UC_21_4 covers detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DELETE to /api/customize/git-repositories/* by non-admin principal with HTTP 200/204 response. Indicates post-exfiltration cleanup or availability impact via authorization bypass.

suggestion.title: Credentials exposed in API response bodies
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'exfiltrate stored Git credentials' from endpoints. Test/get/browseFiles responses should be inspected for plaintext secrets (SSH keys, tokens, API keys).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor responses from /api/customize/git-repositories/*/test, /branches, /files endpoints for regex patterns matching SSH keys (BEGIN RSA/ED25519), GitHub tokens (ghp_), GitLab tokens (glpat-), Azure PATs, or AWS credentials. Any match indicates credential exposure in API responses.

suggestion.title: Formie Hidden Field SSTI Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'crafted values into Hidden fields... were evaluated as Twig during submission handling'—needs signature-based detection for Twig template syntax in form submissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Formie form endpoints for Twig template syntax ({{ }}, {% %}, {# #}) in field values. Flag submissions containing template metacharacters to hidden fields as potential SSTI exploitation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Formie Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patches starting at 2.2.20, indicating versions < 2.2.20 are vulnerable. Required for asset discovery and remediation prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and vulnerability scanners for Formie < 2.2.20. Cross-reference public web applications with Craft CMS fingerprints to identify exposure.

suggestion.title: Craft Application Error Spike Correlated with Form Submissions
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'serious compromise' would result—successful SSTI typically generates exceptions, stack traces, or template parsing errors in application logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate spikes in Craft application errors with form submissions to public Formie endpoints. Look for template syntax errors, undefined variables, or unexpected execution traces.

suggestion.title: Non-Standard Custom Default Values in Hidden Fields
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable configuration as 'Hidden fields (with Default value → Custom)'—this deviates from normal form behavior and represents the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Formie forms with hidden fields configured to use custom default values. This non-standard configuration indicates either misconfiguration or deliberate attacker setup.

suggestion.title: mistralai 2.4.6: import-time child process spawning from Python context
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious code 'executes on import on Linux' but existing UCs don't capture parent-child correlation across import boundary. Need to detect when Python import of mistralai triggers unexpected child processes (shells, curl, Python interpreters) in same process tree.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for parent process = python/python3 (mistralai import context) with child_process in (curl, sh, bash, python*) spawned immediately after import statement or setup.py execution. Establish baseline of normal mistralai import children; alert on process names not typically spawned by legitimate package initialization.

suggestion.title: mistralai 2.4.6: PyPI package upload bypassing Trusted Publishing verification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'the upload bypassed this repository's normal release pipeline (which uses PyPI Trusted Publishing)' and 'No v2.4.6 tag, commit, or release workflow run exists in this repository'. Need to detect unauthorized package uploads or uploads lacking valid CI attestation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PyPI package uploads for 'mistralai' that lack corresponding git tag, release workflow run, or Trusted Publishing attestation token. Cross-correlate version bump (2.4.5 → 2.4.6) against repository commit history; flag uploads with zero matching commits or CI workflows.

suggestion.title: mistralai 2.4.6: curl with TLS verification disabled (-k flag) downloading suspicious archive
suggestion.rationale: UC_13_3 covers the hunt, but missing explicit focus on -k (insecure) flag as behavioral indicator. Article describes 'TLS verification disabled' download. Standalone -k usage in curl is high-confidence malicious signal in legitimate package context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on curl processes (or wget, python -m http.client) spawned from Python context with -k, --insecure, or PYTHONHTTPSVERIFY=0 flags. Correlate with destination IP 83.142.209.194 or .pyz/.tar/.zip file downloads. Establish high confidence if spawned from __init__.py or setup.py file context.

suggestion.title: mistralai 2.4.6: installation of exact malicious package version
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies mistralai==2.4.6 as the malicious version. Need to detect environment-specific marker: pip/conda install of that exact version tuple. Article states 'The mistralai PyPI package version 2.4.6 contains' — specific version is the IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install, conda install, or poetry add commands targeting mistralai==2.4.6 (exact version match). Also detect import statements for mistralai with sys.modules inspection showing version 2.4.6 loaded. Alert with high confidence on any installation or import after 2026-05-18 (article publication date).

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Compromise and Bulk Code Repository Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'stolen GitHub token let hackers steal codebase' and 'hackers have downloaded its source code'; detection opportunity for token misuse patterns and unusual repository clone/download volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API for unusual PAT/token usage including bulk repository clones, high-volume API calls from unexpected locations, or access to repositories not typically queried by service accounts. Correlate with new token creation events.

suggestion.title: VMware ESXi Encryption and Snapshot Disabling by shinysp1d3r
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat actor 'deploys an in-memory tool called shinysp1d3r to encrypt VMware ESXi targets and disable snapshots'; direct IoC for ransomware activity on hypervisor infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shinysp1d3r process execution, unexpected snapshot removal/disabling from vCenter without approval tickets, and subsequent ESXi datastore encryption activity. Monitor for in-memory tool execution patterns and snapshot edit API calls.

suggestion.title: Extortion Gang Activity and Data Leak Portal Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article documents CoinbaseCartel adding victim to 'data leak site (DLS)' and making ransom demand; detection should cover threat intelligence feeds monitoring for victim org appearance on known ransomware portals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement automated dark web/DLS monitoring for organization name, domain, or subsidiary brands appearing on CoinbaseCartel leak portal. Cross-correlate with incoming ransom email patterns, wallet addresses, and known CoinbaseCartel communication templates.

suggestion.title: Phishing and Social Engineering Leading to GitHub Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states gang 'gain access via social engineering, various forms of phishing, and compromised credentials'; detection should target email and endpoint behaviors preceding credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on phishing emails targeting GitHub user accounts or engineers, followed by anomalous GitHub device authorization requests, new PAT creation, or changes to API token scope/permissions within 24 hours. Baseline normal developer tooling patterns.

suggestion.title: Invalidation of Compromised GitHub Access Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'invalidated the compromised credentials'; detection use case for identifying which access tokens were revoked and when, correlating with API activity logs to identify window of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for GitHub API token revocations followed by suspicious activity during the token's active period. Correlate token creation time, first use, last use, and revocation timestamp to establish compromise window and scope of data access.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Infrastructure and CoinbaseCartel DLS Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CoinbaseCartel as responsible actor and notes it consists of 'ShinyHunters and Lapsus$ affiliates'; detection should monitor for infrastructure overlap, communication patterns, and data leak portal interaction signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network egress for connections to known CoinbaseCartel DLS infrastructure, Lapsus$ attributed C2 domains, and ShinyHunters payment processor domains. Alert on DNS queries for data leak portal subdomains or DLS mirrors known to host CoinbaseCartel victim data.

suggestion.title: NGINX Process Executing Unexpected Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes RCE exploitation: 'Hackers Actively Exploiting Critical NGINX RCE Vulnerability.' RCE by definition means shell command execution; defenders need to detect NGINX worker processes spawning shell interpreters or system utilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by nginx, nginx worker, or www-data parent processes (UID/GID match). Alert on shell spawns (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or system utilities (curl, wget, nc) originating from web server process trees.

suggestion.title: NGINX Exploit Payload Signature in Request Logs
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'actively exploiting' suggests delivery mechanism is HTTP requests to NGINX. Payload fingerprinting in access/error logs is the upstream detection point before RCE execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate NGINX error logs for specific CVE payload patterns (memory corruption, buffer overflow, or code injection strings) against 400/500 error codes. Flag requests with unusual query strings, path traversal attempts, or known exploit PoC signatures targeting NGINX.

suggestion.title: NGINX Service Version Enumeration or Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability is version-specific. Article's 'critical' designation implies discrete affected versions. Attacker reconnaissance via banner grabbing or version detection (OPTIONS, HEAD requests) precedes exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for port scanning, repeated HEAD/OPTIONS requests, or User-Agent patterns typical of Nessus/Shodan scanners targeting port 80/443 within 24hrs before successful RCE payload delivery.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Activity from NGINX
