suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on volume-based GitHub operations: bulk .tar.gz/.zip exports of private repos, unusual clone counts from single account/IP, or export of entire repo histories. Correlate timing of large code downloads with subsequent npm package publishes to establish exfil-to-poison pipeline.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection Detection in Installed TanStack Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes TanStack as distribution vector; no UC for runtime detection of injected payloads (spawned processes, network connections, secrets access) in poisoned packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor code imported from node_modules/tanstack/* for unexpected child-process spawning, outbound connections, or environment variable exfiltration. Use entropy/YARA signatures on installed packages. Track TanStack source patterns against baseline to detect injected obfuscated code.

suggestion.title: Grafana Supply-Chain Downstream Impact Assessment via Dependency Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Grafana...TanStack npm Attack' — threat propagates to all packages consuming poisoned TanStack. No UC for detecting malicious transitive dependencies in build pipelines or package lock files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit package.lock and package-lock.json for resolved malicious TanStack versions across internal and customer deployments. Alert when builds include compromised versions. Monitor GitHub Actions for secret access during npm install steps or unexpected post-install scripts.

suggestion.title: Anomalous OneDrive API Activity from Uncommon Clients
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly frames OneDrive as C2 infrastructure. Pipeline missed the detection logic: legitimate endpoints (OneDrive) abuse requires behavioral baselines—spike in upload/download volume, API calls at off-hours, or from abnormal geographic locations. Article establishes 'command-and-control' as the attack phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Graph API and OneDrive REST API calls for access patterns inconsistent with user baseline: large data transfers, POST/PUT during off-hours, or authentication from impossible geographies. Correlate with process execution that rarely touches cloud services.

suggestion.title: Stolen or Leaked OneDrive OAuth Tokens Used for C2
suggestion.rationale: OneDrive-as-C2 implies either compromised user credentials or stolen OAuth tokens. Article does not specify initial access vector, but token theft is the probable persistence mechanism. 'Valid Accounts' (T1078.004) and 'Application Access Token' (T1550.001) are canonical MITRE techniques for cloud C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual Graph API token acquisition (out-of-band consent flows, suspicious redirect URIs), token reuse across mismatched device/location contexts, or token refresh patterns inconsistent with user behavior. Flag consent grants for OneDrive scopes from known-malicious IPs or impossible-travel scenarios.

suggestion.title: Process-to-OneDrive Communication (GraphWorm Lateral Execution)
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'GraphWorm malware,' implying process execution on compromised systems that communicates with OneDrive for command delivery. Pipeline ignored entirely. Detect processes spawning uncommon HTTP/HTTPS connections to graph.microsoft.com or onedrive.com—especially unsigned or recently-dropped binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process creation (unsigned binary, temp directory origin, or rare name) with outbound connections to graph.microsoft.com or onedrive.com on ports 80/443. Flag if process has no history of cloud API interaction. Enrich with DNS timestamps and TLS certificate anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unusual File Sharing and Delegation Changes in OneDrive (Persistence/Exfil)
suggestion.rationale: OneDrive C2 implies malware capability to read/write/share files and modify permissions. Article title does not exclude exfiltration; this is canonical data-exfil pattern for cloud-resident C2. Pipeline missed collection and exfiltration phase mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OneDrive for abnormal sharing patterns: bulk file shares to new external domains, sharing permission escalations (view→edit), or anonymous link creation in rapid succession. Correlate with failed sign-in attempts or token-based logins preceding the share events.

suggestion.title: GraphWorm Malware Hash and File Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'GraphWorm' as the malware. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Should identify hashes, file paths, registry keys, or command-line signatures unique to GraphWorm samples if disclosed in the body (truncated here, but standard in threat intel releases).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for GraphWorm-specific file artifacts: hashes from public samples, DLL injection patterns, or registry persistence keys. Alert if binary detects as low-confidence AV (defense evasion via obfuscation common in cloud C2 malware).

suggestion.title: MSHTA Execution with Suspicious Script Arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Hackers Abuse MSHTA Legacy Windows Tool'—direct statement of attack vector. MSHTA spawning with script/URL arguments is the entry point; pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mshta.exe execution with script arguments, encoded payloads, or remote URLs. MSHTA is a legitimate LOLBin frequently abused to execute HTML/VBScript while evading application whitelists. Flag any mshta.exe spawning with /e, /s, or http/file:// arguments.

suggestion.title: MSHTA Child Process Spawning and Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware is 'Deliver[ed]' via MSHTA—requires execution step. Pipeline failed to map malware execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate mshta.exe process creation with spawned child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe). Malware droppers delivered via MSHTA typically establish execution context immediately. Alert on mshta parent process with suspicious child cmdlines or binary writes.

suggestion.title: LummaStealer Credential Access and Memory Scraping
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'LummaStealer'—a known info-stealer malware. Pipeline extracted zero malware family recognition and missed credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: LummaStealer targets credential managers, browser databases, and clipboard. Detect suspicious process access to lsass.exe, WinLogon credential cache, or bulk SQLite reads from browser profiles. Monitor for credential dumping patterns and unauthorized sensitive data reads.

suggestion.title: Amatera Malware Persistence and Registry Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Amatera' as delivery payload. Zero IOC extraction or persistence-phase mapping despite clear malware naming.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Amatera likely establishes persistence via HKLM/HKCU Run registry keys or scheduled tasks. Monitor for suspicious registry writes post-MSHTA execution, unsigned binaries in startup locations, or scheduled task creation with script-based commands.

suggestion.title: Malware C2 Communication and Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Stealer malware delivery implies C2 callbacks and data exfiltration. Pipeline missed command-and-control and exfiltration phases entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from mshta.exe or child processes to suspicious domains. LummaStealer exfiltrates credentials and sensitive data over HTTPS. Detect anomalous C2 patterns: high-frequency reconnections, large data transfers, or known stealer C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Go Module Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'single-letter Go module typosquat.' Pipeline extracted zero module IOCs. Detection should flag suspiciously short/similar module names (e.g., single-character names like 'u' masquerading as 'uuid') being imported or installed during builds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor `go get` and `go mod` operations for typosquatted module names (single-char or homoglyph variants of popular libraries). Flag imports from less-trusted registries. Cross-reference module publish date against org's first-seen timestamp to identify zero-day typosquats.

suggestion.title: Go Process Initiating Anomalous DNS Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'DNS-based backdoor'—pipeline missed entire C2 phase and corresponding detection surface. Go runtime processes should not be initiating arbitrary DNS queries to external infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Go processes (go.exe, compiled Go binaries) performing DNS lookups to non-allowlisted domains. Flag beaconing patterns: periodic DNS queries to same subdomain, DNS tunneling indicators (high subdomain entropy, unusual query volume), or queries to known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Go Module Dependency in Build Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack succeeds when malicious module enters dependency tree. Article context implies build-time compromise—go.mod/go.sum files should be audited for suspicious new entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor changes to go.mod/go.sum files in git commits. Flag addition of modules not in organizational dependency allowlist. Correlate module author reputation, publish date, and download counts to identify zero-day or unpopular typosquats. Alert on modules added outside normal dependency-management processes.

suggestion.title: Single-Character Go Package Name Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'single-letter' as typosquat technique—extremely rare in legitimate Go ecosystem. Direct pattern match on module registry logs should yield high-confidence detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Go package registry (pkg.go.dev, proxy.golang.org) logs for module imports matching regex ^[a-z]$. Cross-reference against curated list of legitimate single-character modules (minimal/empty). Flag all matches as typosquatting attempts. Enrich with author email, module metadata, and first-published timestamp.

suggestion.title: Malicious Go Binary Execution from Build Context
suggestion.rationale: Typosquatted module imports execute attacker code at build-time via init() or build-time hooks. Process execution from build tools should trigger forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process execution spawned from Go build tools, package managers, or IDE contexts. Flag child processes with unusual parents (e.g., go.exe spawning system utilities, network tools, or credential-access binaries). Correlate with go.mod changes to link execution to new module imports.

suggestion.title: FsTx Malicious File Creation on USB/EFI Partition Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes attack vector: 'placing specially crafted FsTx files on a USB drive or EFI partition' as exploitation prerequisite. No detection use case generated despite this being the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FsTx-prefixed file creation on removable media or EFI system partitions. Baseline legitimate autofstx.exe auto-recovery activity. Alert on suspicious FsTx variants created outside Windows patch windows, correlate with subsequent WinRE environment transition within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: WinRE Boot Transition to Unrestricted Shell Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation sequence: 'rebooting into WinRE, and then triggering a shell with unrestricted access to the BitLocker-protected storage volume by holding down the CTRL key.' WinRE-to-shell transitions require behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected WinRE environment boots followed by cmd.exe or powershell.exe process creation with SYSTEM privileges in WinRE context. Baseline legitimate administrative recovery boots and alert on anomalous boot sequences outside change-management windows with shell spawning.

suggestion.title: autofstx.exe Removal from Session Manager BootExecute Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article states Microsoft mitigation requires 'removing the autofstx.exe entry from the Session Manager's BootExecute REG_MULTI_SZ value.' Attackers exploiting YellowKey may remove or modify this registry value to enable persistent WinRE access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\BootExecute for deletion of autofstx.exe entries or substitution with unsigned executables. Detect both direct registry edits and PowerShell modifications. Alert on winpeshl.ini deletion from WinRE image directories.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Configuration Downgrade to TPM-Only Mode
suggestion.rationale: Article mitigation states: 'configure BitLocker on already encrypted devices from TPM-only mode to TPM+PIN mode' requiring 'a pre-boot PIN to decrypt the drive at startup.' Reverse configuration (removal of PIN requirement) indicates YellowKey exploitation preparation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BitLocker mode downgrades removing pre-boot PIN requirement or downgrading from TPM+PIN to TPM-only. Detect via registry (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\FVE), WMI queries, or Intune drift. Correlate with FsTx file creation and WinRE boot events within 1-hour window.

suggestion.title: Multi-Zero-Day Correlation Chain: BlueHammer, RedSun, GreenPlasma, UnDefend
suggestion.rationale: Article discloses researcher 'Nightmare Eclipse' leaked five related zero-days in coordinated protest. Article explicitly notes 'BlueHammer and RedSun local privilege escalation zero-day flaws, both of which are now being exploited in attacks.' Detection must correlate across all five for sophisticated compromise identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish correlation rule across five zero-day exploitation signatures: (1) YellowKey FsTx files + WinRE boot, (2) BlueHammer LPE process patterns, (3) RedSun LPE indicators, (4) GreenPlasma SYSTEM elevation, (5) UnDefend Defender update blocks (Event ID 3002). Alert on 2+ detections within 1 hour as indicator of multi-exploit attack chain.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Definition Update Blocking (UnDefend Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies UnDefend as zero-day where 'attackers with standard user permissions can exploit to block Microsoft Defender definition updates.' This defense-evasion technique enables post-compromise malware persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows Defender operational logs for repeated definition update failures. Baseline legitimate delays (network, offline systems). Alert on sustained update blockage from single system within 24 hours, particularly when correlated with other zero-day exploitation indicators or privilege elevation events.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Remote Code Execution via Public Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'PoC Exploit Released for PostgreSQL RCE'—explicit signal of execution phase via publicly disclosed exploit. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite unambiguous kill-chain trigger in headline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process spawning from PostgreSQL daemon (postgres, psql, pgbench) — particularly shells (bash, sh, cmd, powershell) or interpreters (python, perl). Correlate timing with connection logs. Flag execution context changes where postgres UID spawns non-database utilities.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Suspicious Outbound Network Connection
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploitation typically followed by C2 communication or data exfiltration. Title phrase 'PoC Exploit Released' signals active exploitation scenarios requiring post-compromise detection. Zero network-based use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline PostgreSQL process network behavior (replication, backups to known hosts). Alert on postgres/psql processes connecting to non-standard ports, external IP ranges, or anomalous geolocation. Flag bi-directional traffic patterns consistent with C2.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection or Command Injection in PostgreSQL Logs
suggestion.rationale: RCE in PostgreSQL typically delivered via SQL injection or unsafe function calls (COPY, EXECUTE variants). Title mentions RCE but article body unreadable—pipeline should still generate injection-pattern detection from the known attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan PostgreSQL logs for SQL injection signatures: quotes escaping, comment sequences (--), union-based payloads, base64-encoded chunks in WHERE clauses, use of dangerous functions (CREATE LANGUAGE plpythonu, COPY, EXECUTE). Alert on malformed protocol or version-specific exploit patterns.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Privilege Escalation or Unauthorized Authentication
suggestion.rationale: 20-year-old vulnerability may involve auth bypass or privilege confusion. Title provides no details but known RCE patterns in legacy PostgreSQL often root in privilege mishandling or role confusion. Zero privilege-escalation detection UCs generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed authentication attempts with unusual role names (e.g., 'postgres' from non-administrative source, or root-like role creation). Track role permission grants before/after suspicious connection. Alert on superuser privilege assignments to non-DBA accounts.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Version Detection and CVE Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'PostgreSQL' RCE but provides no CVE ID or specific version. Pipeline extracted zero metadata (CVE, affected versions, CVSS). Should correlate live PostgreSQL version against known 20+ year old RCE CVEs (e.g., CVE-2004-0977 buffer overflow) and scan for exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract PostgreSQL version from server logs, connection banners, or diagnostic queries. Cross-reference against CVE database for RCE vulnerabilities. Generate signatures for known exploit delivery methods targeting the identified version. Alert if exposed instance version matches known vulnerable releases.

suggestion.title: Malvertising-Delivered Trojanized Productivity App Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article description states pipeline analyzes 'trojanized productivity apps and malvertising to deliver stealthy payloads.' This is the primary infection vector and should trigger detection UC covering malvertising payload delivery and suspicious productivity app launch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on productivity application (Word, Excel, PDF reader) execution from unusual paths (temp dirs, downloads, AppData/Local/Temp) combined with parent process being browser or network-delivery utility. Flag unusual network connectivity from productivity app to non-standard ports immediately post-execution.

suggestion.title: Certificate Reuse Across Malware Clusters
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Certificate ... Reuse' as tracking mechanism. This indicates TamperedChef clusters are linked via shared SSL/TLS certificates, enabling both clustering and detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track unique certificate thumbprints/issuer combinations across malicious C2 domains. Flag IPs/domains presenting certificates used by known TamperedChef C2 infrastructure or sharing certificate issuer+validity window with known malware cluster samples.

suggestion.title: Code Reuse Clustering via Malware Binary Similarity
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'Code Reuse' as detection technique for clustering TamperedChef variants. Suggests fuzzy-hash or disassembly-level similarity linking variants like DocuFlex and EvilAI.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor binary uploads and endpoint detections for malware samples with high fuzzy-hash similarity (SSDEEP, tlsh) to known TamperedChef variants (DocuFlex, EvilAI, CL-CRI-1089, CL-UNK-1090). Flag clusters of samples sharing code blocks but differing in packaging or delivery method.

suggestion.title: Remote Access Trojan (RAT) Command-and-Control Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords and description identify TamperedChef as Remote Access Trojan; article implies C2 callback capability. Detection UC needed for post-execution network beaconing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained outbound connections from trojanized productivity app process to unusual external IPs/domains. Flag DNS queries for suspicious TLDs or domains matching known C2 infrastructure patterns. Monitor for beaconing behavior: periodic callbacks at fixed intervals post-execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Productivity Application Capability Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: RATs typically discover system configuration post-execution (OS version, installed software, user/domain info). Detection UC should cover discovery phase unique to trojanized productivity apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor productivity app processes (spawned child processes executing net.exe, whoami.exe, tasklist.exe, reg.exe query) for system enumeration. Flag unusual registry queries by Word/Excel/AdobeReader. Alert on WMI queries spawned from productivity app parent process.

suggestion.title: Staged Delivery from Certificate-Signed Malware Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article links TamperedChef via shared certificates; suggests infrastructure used for multi-stage delivery. Detection should cover secondary payload staging from C2 using same certificate infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned by trojanized app making outbound HTTPS connections to IPs presenting certificates matching TamperedChef cluster signature (issuer, validity, thumbprint). Flag file writes to disk post-connection followed by child process execution.

suggestion.title: EchoCreep/GraphWorm Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names EchoCreep and GraphWorm backdoors; no detection use case for identifying their execution. Article headline establishes these are the primary malware families being deployed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of processes named or containing 'echocreep', 'graphworm', or associated obfuscated variants. Correlate with file write events to temp directories immediately preceding network C2 activity to Discord or Graph API endpoints. Focus on execution from email client temp folders and startup-run keys.

suggestion.title: Discord Webhook C2 Communication from Enterprise Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes Discord as primary C2 channel ('Deploys...Using Discord'); zero detection use case for Discord API abuse. Threat uses legitimate Discord API for command control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTPS traffic to Discord API endpoints (discordapp.com, discord.com) from non-browser processes or from SYSTEM/NETWORK SERVICE. Correlate with outbound POST requests to /api/webhooks/ paths and inbound webhook message parsing within 10 seconds. Exclude Discord client and authorized applications.

suggestion.title: Anomalous MS Graph API Tokens and Delegated Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names MS Graph API as attack vector ('Using...MS Graph API'); no detection for unauthorized Graph API token acquisition or scope escalation. This is the persistence and lateral-movement mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect grant of Mail.Send, Mail.ReadWrite, or User.ReadAll permissions to unexpected applications. Alert on Azure AD sign-in events with suspicious app IDs requesting graph.microsoft.com scopes immediately after user clicks phishing link. Correlate with subsequent large-volume /me/sendMail API calls within 15 minutes of token grant.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Operations via MS Graph sendMail API
suggestion.rationale: MS Graph API abuse described in title implies mass email campaign; no detection use case for identifying Graph API sendMail abuse pattern. 'Deploys' in title suggests propagation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >100 sendMail or sendAsUser API calls from single Azure AD service principal or user within 10-minute window. Correlate Graph API request logs with outbound mail transport rules or forwarding rule additions. Flag requests originating from non-corporate IPs or Tor exit nodes.

suggestion.title: Webworm Threat Actor Initial Access Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'Webworm' as threat actor name; zero use cases for detecting initial compromise vector. Attack chain begins with credential compromise or phishing; no detection for entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline: detect user OAuth consent screen approvals for unfamiliar applications requesting Mail/Graph scopes within 5 minutes of phishing email delivery (indicated by URLClickEventAction in MDO logs). Flag if approved app is new, unverified, or requests excessive permissions. Correlate timestamp with subsequent token issuance and immediate Graph API activity.

suggestion.title: Webworm Malware Family Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'Webworm'; threat intelligence lacks detection for its indicators. Malware family name should map to file hashes, registry keys, injection patterns, or network signatures absent from article body due to corruption. Minimum viable extraction: file drops to %TEMP%, mutex creation, scheduled task persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry writes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run containing 'webworm' or 'echocreep'; file creation in %TEMP%\webworm* or %APPDATA% with .vbs or .ps1 extension; Task Scheduler task creation with Discord webhook in command line. Baseline on malware sandbox detections to extract PE imphash.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Authorization Code Phishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Comment explicitly describes compromise vector: 'employee shouldn't have clicked to view the shared document they got through email. And definitely shouldn't have copy & pasted the authorization code that most likely gave them access to their Auth Token for Salesforce.' This is the initial compromise mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for phishing emails containing Salesforce OAuth authorization code lures (e.g., 'verify identity', 'confirm access', 'authorize app'). Flag emails with shortened URLs, 'authorize' buttons, or copy-paste instructions. Correlate email recipients with successful Salesforce token generation events within 2 hours of email delivery.

suggestion.title: Bulk Franchisee Document Export from Salesforce
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'gained access to certain 7-Eleven systems used to store franchisee documents' and ShinyHunters 'stolen over 600,000 records.' Indicates systematic collection phase targeting document storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Salesforce document access patterns. Alert on single accounts exporting >300 franchisee documents within 1 hour, accounts accessing multiple franchisee ORGs not previously contacted, or cascading reads of sensitive objects followed by archive creation events.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Salesforce Account Access Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Breach occurred April 8, 2026 via stolen Salesforce credentials. Detection should identify account compromise indicators: unusual geography, off-hours access, API token generation by non-admin users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce login events for geographically impossible travel, logins from high-risk proxies or TOR exit nodes, off-hours access by desk workers, rapid API calls immediately after successful login, and access to sensitive object types by non-manager accounts.

suggestion.title: Large Data Archive Creation and Exfiltration (9.4GB Threshold)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters leaked a 9.4GB archive of documents on their dark web leak site.' Exfiltration phase indicator is the creation and bulk transfer of encrypted/compressed archive files off-network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large archive creation (tar.gz, 7z, zip >500MB) on systems with Salesforce console access. Monitor egress to cloud storage (Dropbox, AWS S3, Mega) and anonymization infrastructure (Tor, residential proxy). Flag encrypted tunnels exfiltrating >500MB in <4 hours correlated with Salesforce data access.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Leak Site Monitoring for 7-Eleven Data
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters leaked a 9.4GB archive of documents on their dark web leak site after the company refused to pay a ransom.' Threat intelligence must monitor breach forums and extortion boards for advertised datasets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Subscribe to dark-web breach board monitoring for 7-Eleven, Salesforce, or franchisee-related data advertisements. Ingest alerts from ShinyHunters leak site scraping. Cross-reference exposed data with internal PII inventory. Generate customer notification and breach timeline artifacts.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing Against Exposed Salesforce Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Post-breach context: ShinyHunters extracted 600K+ records and 9.4GB archive. Secondary attacks should use exposed credentials for lateral movement or re-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-disclosure, monitor Salesforce login attempts from credential databases matching the exposed 600K records. Flag failed login bursts on leaked employee accounts, successful logins from new geographies, and secondary lateral movement from Salesforce to downstream services (AWS, Slack, Google Workspace) using compromised credentials.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Repository Compromise - Malicious Tag Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'All Tags Point to Imposter Commit.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs for the compromised repository (actions-cool/issues-helper) and did not model tag-level persistence as an attack phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor public GitHub Actions repositories for tag mutations—specifically, tags that are re-pointed to different commits, unsigned tags, or tags authored by accounts outside the repository organization. Cross-reference tag commit hashes against release notes and changelogs to identify orphaned/forged tags.

suggestion.title: Compromised Public GitHub Action Downloaded and Executed in CI/CD Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Title confirms action is compromised; supply-chain attack vector is execution in consuming workflows. Pipeline did not generate use case for detecting workflow invocation of malicious actions-cool/issues-helper versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions workflows that invoke actions-cool/issues-helper or other public actions, especially with non-pinned versions or major-version-only refs. Correlate with commits that added or updated the action reference. Flag actions pulled during time-window of compromise across all consuming repositories.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from GitHub Actions Environment - CI/CD Secrets Access
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Exfiltrates CI/CD Credentials.' Pipeline did not model credential exfiltration as a detection use case, nor extract indicators of the exfiltration target (URL, IP, domain).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect actions accessing GitHub-provided secrets (GITHUB_TOKEN, custom secrets) and subsequently making outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections, especially to non-GitHub hosts. Flag actions that base64-encode or otherwise obfuscate credentials in logs, or that instantiate curl/wget commands with credential arguments.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Integrity Check - Public Action Signature and Commit Verification
suggestion.rationale: Malicious commit persisted across all tags because verification is insufficient. Pipeline did not suggest detection for workflows that fail to validate action GPG signatures or commit hashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enforce and audit cryptographic verification of public GitHub Actions: validate GPG-signed tags, verify commit hashes match expected values, check author key fingerprints against trusted registries. Alert on workflows using loose refs (e.g., `@v1` instead of `@v1.2.3`), unsigned tags, or tags signed by keys outside organizational trust anchor.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Connections from CI/CD Runner Environment
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration implies outbound network traffic carrying credentials. Pipeline did not model detection for unexpected egress from GitHub Actions runners or CI/CD execution environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress from GitHub Actions runners to non-whitelisted destinations. Alert on connections to newly-registered domains, IP space owned by threat-actor infrastructure, or known credential-exfiltration services. Correlate connection timing with workflow steps that access secrets or environment variables.

suggestion.title: Repository Audit Log for Unexpected Tag Creation or Modification Events
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates attackers modified all tags to point to malicious commit. Pipeline did not suggest detection for GitHub audit events showing unauthorized tag manipulation or branch protection bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository audit logs for create/update/delete events on tags, especially in public actions repositories. Alert on tags modified after initial release, branches created with suspicious naming patterns, or branch protection rules disabled. Correlate with commit authorship anomalies (unexpected authors, service accounts).

suggestion.title: node-ipc Malicious Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'node-ipc' as malicious package published to npm; attack vector is 'npm supply chain.' Pipeline extracted zero package names despite this being primary IOC surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm.exe, npm.cmd, and yarn process execution for 'install node-ipc' arguments or package.json modifications adding node-ipc dependency. Alert on lock file changes (package-lock.json, yarn.lock) reflecting node-ipc versions outside known-safe baseline. Flag installations from non-official registries or mirror fallback behavior during resolution.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Payload Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malicious versions' suggesting code execution payload. npm packages execute postinstall hooks during installation — pipeline did not map to execution phase or detect install-time process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from npm install lifecycle (node.exe, npm.exe, powershell.exe, cmd.exe). Alert on postinstall/preinstall hooks containing obfuscated commands, external URL downloads, or network calls. Monitor for scripts executing in node_modules/.bin/, .npm/_cacache, or global npm directories with suspicious command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: node-ipc Module Code Execution via require()
suggestion.rationale: Installed malicious package executes when imported. Article does not detail mechanism but is inherent to npm supply-chain attacks. Pipeline did not generate detection for module require() or import execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned from Node.js applications requiring node-ipc module. Correlate package installation event with subsequent unexpected process execution within minutes. Alert on unusual file access from node_modules/node-ipc directories followed by network or credential access events.

suggestion.title: Outbound Command-and-Control from Compromised Developer Machine

suggestion.title: Service Account Privilege Escalation via Elevation of Privilege CVEs

suggestion.title: Process Execution Spoofing Legitimate Software Names with Code-Signed Binaries

suggestion.title: Oyster Malware Loader and Ransomware Deployment Chain

Flag hosts running vulnerable versions and correlate with HTTP access patterns to determine if traversal exploitation is occurring.

suggestion.title: Installation of malicious guardrails-ai==0.10.1 PyPI package (CVE-2026-45758)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'an attacker published a malicious version of guardrails-ai (0.10.1) to PyPI' and 'any user who installed guardrails-ai==0.10.1 from PyPI on May 11, 2026' — direct artifact for package installation detection via pip/uv/poetry logs and Python package manager records.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for pip/uv/poetry install commands targeting guardrails-ai with exact version 0.10.1, correlate to install timestamps on/after May 11, 2026. Check pip freeze output, site-packages, and requirements.txt files for post-incident asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Python process executing transformers.pyz payload from git-tanstack.com
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'transformers.pyz' as malicious executable staged on TeamPCP C2 domain — represents secondary payload delivery and execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Python (python.exe, python3, pythonw.exe) spawning with command-line references to .pyz files named 'transformers.pyz'. Correlate process start time with network connections to git-tanstack.com or 83.142.209.194.

suggestion.title: DNS query for git-tanstack.com TeamPCP C2 staging domain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'git-tanstack.com' as 'TeamPCP C2 staging domain' and maps to IP 83.142.209.194. DNS is earliest indicator of C2 intent before C2 connection establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt DNS query logs for git-tanstack.com or suspicious subdomains. Flag any response matching 83.142.209.194. High confidence if preceded by Python process execution within same host session.

suggestion.title: Outbound network connection to TeamPCP C2 infrastructure 83.142.209.194
suggestion.rationale: Article names 83.142.209.194 as C2 IP address (defanged notation provided). Direct network-layer C2 detection, especially high-confidence if source is Python process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound TCP/UDP connections to 83.142.209.194 from any source. Escalate confidence if: (a) source is Python interpreter, (b) connection established within 24h of guardrails-ai==0.10.1 install, or (c) preceded by git-tanstack.com DNS query.

suggestion.title: Malicious package installer spawning command shells or scripting engines
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks commonly abuse pip/poetry processes to spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or wscript.exe. Article context: PyPI package installation as attack vector suggests payload execution via interpreter child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip.exe, pip3.exe, poetry.exe, uv.exe for spawning shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe, wscript.exe) or network utilities (curl.exe, wget, nc.exe). Baseline normal package install behavior to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability asset exposure: guardrails-ai ≤0.10.1 installed on endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'any user who installed guardrails-ai==0.10.1' and notes incident window (May 11). Post-compromise remediation requires asset inventory of installed vulnerable package versions across environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Python site-packages, pip list, poetry.lock, requirements.txt, and pip cache for guardrails-ai package in versions ≤0.10.1. Cross-reference install dates with May 11-12 incident window. Identify systems requiring remediation.

suggestion.title: Burst of azure-instance-identity POSTs (vmId enumeration / forged PKCS#7)
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: attacker sends POST requests to '/api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity' with forged vmId values in malicious PKCS#7 message to bypass signature validation. UC_19_2 provided in body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-volume POST requests to /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity from single source within 10-minute windows. Forged PKCS#7 exploitation attempts will generate repeated requests as attacker enumerates target vmIds.

suggestion.title: Agent token redemption: PKCS#7 bypass POST followed by credential exfiltration GET
suggestion.rationale: Article attack chain: attacker exploits signature bypass to steal workspace agent session token, then redeems token by accessing gitsshkey or external-auth endpoints. UC_19_3 in body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST to /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity with subsequent GET to /api/v2/workspaceagents/me/gitsshkey or /api/v2/workspaceagents/me/external-auth from same source within 30 minutes to detect token theft and immediate credential harvesting.

suggestion.title: Coder v2 vulnerable software inventory (CVE-2026-46354 exposure)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability affects Coder v2 workspaceagents service with no authentication required. UC_19_4 provides asset discovery hunt targeting vulnerable instance identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Coder v2 software instances via vulnerability datamodel or software inventory. Prioritize network-facing systems and correlate with patch status to determine exposure scope.

suggestion.title: OAuth2 consent abuse post-token theft
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_OAUTH_ABUSE hunt — attacker possessing stolen agent token can perform unauthorized OAuth grants and app role assignments to establish persistence or escalate privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OAuth2PermissionGrant, consent-to-application, or delegated permission grant events originating from IP addresses or user contexts correlated with azureidentity exploitation patterns.

suggestion.title: HAXcms: Extraction of Hardcoded HMAC Key from Source/Config (T1552.001)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'hardcoded HMAC Key (line 2160)' and 'passes the literal string "0"'. Attack begins by extracting this credential. Pipeline produced zero phase/UC entries covering credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reads of HAXcms utility/auth modules (particularly function definitions around line 2160) and config files storing HMAC keys. Correlate with subsequent token-forgery requests to the same target using the extracted key.

suggestion.title: HAXcms: JWT Signature Validation Failures or Admin-Claim Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'forge arbitrary admin-level JSON Web Tokens'. No pipeline UC detected this privilege-escalation indicator. Detection must target JWT validation anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when HAXcms logs JWT signature validation failures or when admin-role claims appear in request contexts (user IDs, source IPs, timestamps) that violate admin-user baselines. Threshold: 3+ validation failures from same source within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: HAXcms: State-Changing Requests to Protected Admin Endpoints via Forged Claims
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact phase: 'full admin access with a single HTTP request' to protected endpoints. No UC detected unauthorized state changes (POST/PUT/DELETE) initiated by non-admin or external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH to {saveOutline,saveManifest,saveNode,createSite,deleteSite,saveFile,saveUser} endpoints where requester is either unauthenticated, external-sourced, or claims non-admin roles. Enforce that these endpoints require valid admin JWT with matching request pattern.

suggestion.title: HAXcms: Automated Extraction of /system/api/connectionSettings from Unknown Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article attack vector: 'unauthenticated attacker' retrieving '/system/api/connectionSettings' to extract HMAC key. This is reconnaissance + exploitation. Pipeline generated no phase entries for exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: High-frequency or repeated GET requests to /system/api/connectionSettings endpoint from unknown/external source IPs with successful (200) responses. Baseline legitimate polling; alert when request rate or source diversity deviates.

suggestion.title: HAXcms: Package Version Inventory — @haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs < 25.0.1
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerable package version constraint. Pipeline extraction returned empty IOCs{}. Threat actor would target systems with <=25.0.0; detection via software inventory is first-line defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset inventory scan for presence of @haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs versions 0.0.1 through 25.0.0 across Node.js package managers (npm, yarn, pnpm lock files) and runtime package-list inspection. Flag for immediate patching to 25.0.1+.

suggestion.title: HAXcms: Sequential Exploitation Chain Correlation — GET key + POST admin (Forged JWT)
suggestion.rationale: Two-step attack sequence described in article: step 1='extract HMAC key', step 2='forge JWT + admin write'. No pipeline UC explicitly correlated both phases in single detection. UC_33_3 attempted this but conflated with file-system noise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when same source IP executes GET /system/api/connectionSettings with 200 response, followed within 5 minutes by POST/PUT/DELETE to any admin endpoint, especially if request patterns suggest automated tooling (identical user-agent, sub-second inter-request timing, rapid endpoint enumeration).

suggestion.title: Malicious npm package installation (@opensearch-project/opensearch 3.5.3, 3.6.2, 3.7.0, 3.8.0)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'external actor gaining force-push permissions...to embed malicious packages into four release versions.' UC_35_2 fully provided in article with Splunk and Defender KQL but pipeline failed to extract.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm.exe, yarn.exe, pnpm.exe, npx.exe execution for installation of @opensearch-project/opensearch with versions 3.5.3, 3.6.2, 3.7.0, or 3.8.0 in command line. Alert on exact version matches as they represent delivery of known-compromised package.

suggestion.title: Postinstall script execution from malicious OpenSearch package
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious payload embedded in npm package; UC_35_5 explicitly provided in article but pipeline failed to extract. Malware executes via postinstall hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by node.exe or npm.exe where InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains @opensearch-project/opensearch and child process spawns cmd.exe, PowerShell, bash, curl, wget, certutil, or bitsadmin.

suggestion.title: On-disk presence of malicious OpenSearch payload by file hash
suggestion.rationale: Article lists three SHA256 hashes under 'Indicators of Compromise (high-fidelity only).' UC_35_3 with complete KQL and Splunk provided but pipeline failed to extract.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DeviceFileEvents where SHA256 matches any of the three malicious hashes. Correlate with node_modules/@opensearch-project/opensearch directory paths to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: C2 beacon to Mini Shai-Hulud/TeamPCP domains (api.masscan.cloud, git-tanstack.com, *.getsession.org)
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_35_4 title attributes C2 to Mini Shai-Hulud/TeamPCP and lists four malicious domains. Complete detection with Splunk and Defender KQL provided but pipeline failed to extract.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections for api.masscan.cloud, git-tanstack.com, filev2.getsession.org, seed1.getsession.org. Correlate with systems matching OpenSearch installation detection window (2026-05-12 onwards).

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration over C2 channel
suggestion.rationale: Article includes T1041 (Exfiltration Over C2 Channel) and T1568 (Dynamic Resolution) in MITRE technique list but no explicit exfiltration hunt provided. Likely phase following successful C2 establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume or anomalous data transfers egressing to the four C2 domains, particularly DNS exfiltration patterns (high-entropy subdomains, base32/base64 encoding) or suspicious HTTP GET/POST parameters containing encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45829 Exploitation Attempt via Model Settings Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'attacker can send a crafted request to force ChromaDB to load a malicious model' with embedded settings before authentication. No detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ChromaDB API endpoints for POST/PUT requests containing model configuration parameters (trust_remote_code, model_name, repo_id) sent to endpoints marked as requiring authentication. Correlate with subsequent child process spawning or outbound connections to huggingface.co domain within 2 seconds of request receipt.

suggestion.title: Hugging Face Model Load Before Authentication Check
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'authentication is only performed after that step, bypassing security' and 'by the time it fires, the model has already been fetched and executed.' No detection for out-of-order authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS connections from ChromaDB process (python/fastapi) to huggingface.co (resolver.huggingface.co, cdn-lfs.huggingface.co) that occur without prior successful HTTP 200 response from /auth or /verify endpoints. Track model artifact downloads >10MB in absence of valid session token.

suggestion.title: ChromaDB HTTP 500 Response Following Model Load Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes end-state: 'The server rejects the request, returns a 500, and the attacker's payload has already run.' This is the forensic signature post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP 500 responses from ChromaDB API endpoints with prior model-loading requests (high entropy repo_id parameters, trust_remote_code=true) and subsequent unexpected child process creation (git, python, bash) or file writes in /tmp or process-owned directories within 1 second of 500 response.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable ChromaDB Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'was introduced in ChromaDB 1.0.0 and was unpatched in version 1.5.8' and deployment risk affects '73% of internet-exposed instances.' Pipeline should flag deployments by version.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify ChromaDB processes or container images with version strings 1.0.0 through 1.5.8 via pip show, pip list, requirements.txt parsing, or Dockerfile inspection. Flag any exposed over HTTP via netstat/ss listening on port 8000 (default) or via AWS/GCP public IP enumeration.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed ChromaDB API Server Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'the PyPI package...is at risk when servers are accessible over HTTP' and cites Shodan data: '73% of internet-exposed instances are running vulnerable version.' No discovery-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for ChromaDB FastAPI services listening on 0.0.0.0:8000 or publicly routable IPs. Check HTTP response headers for 'uvicorn', 'fastapi', or X-Powered-By: FastAPI. Correlate with presence of vulnerable version 1.0.0–1.5.8 and log unauthenticated POST/GET requests to /api/v1/* endpoints.

suggestion.title: Malicious Model Download from Hugging Face During ChromaDB Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'attacker can send a crafted request to force ChromaDB to load a malicious model from the Hugging Face platform and execute it locally.' Network-level model retrieval is the attack transport.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS to huggingface.co/*/resolve/main or cdn-lfs.huggingface.co initiated by ChromaDB process without corresponding user-initiated deployment workflow. Flag concurrent downloads >50MB + child process spawning (git clone, python -m, bash, curl) as post-download artifact staging.
